memory_update.text: For ecommerce_retail_media_data, add CART, EBAY, UBER, EXPE, and CRTO as direct or adjacent US-listed candidates; CRTO should carry a below-1B exception flag.
The node is best mapped as a monetization layer on top of consumer intent: owned transaction data, sponsored ranking, seller/brand ad spend, checkout attribution, and marketplace/retailer APIs.

Obvious leaders AMZN and WMT were not included in the 5-name candidate cap for this pass because the search focus favored less obvious second-order beneficiaries; they remain benchmark comparables for ad scale, closed-loop data, and margin contribution.

Next pass should test additional nodes: SHOP as merchant operating system/Shop Campaigns, TTD as open-web retail-media demand-side infrastructure, ROKU/VZIO/WMT CTV-commerce data, and consumer brands highly exposed to marketplace ad taxes.

node: Ecommerce marketplaces, retail media networks, first-party shopper data, and search/ranking algorithms
summary: Expanded universe emphasizes companies that monetize consumer intent at or near checkout rather than generic ecommerce sellers. The strongest underappreciated mappings are grocery/restaurant delivery ad surfaces, travel-media inventory, seller-funded marketplace ads, and retail-media enablement software. Obvious leaders such as Amazon and Walmart remain primary benchmarks, but this pass focuses on adjacent or second-order beneficiaries where retail media, sponsored ranking, APIs, and closed-loop measurement may be less central in market narratives.
